issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting guidance about the order of attributes to use in the Lecture constructor: the textual task list enumerates attributes in one order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) while the UML diagram shows a different attribute order (numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors). The instructions explicitly ask students to follow the UML order for the constructor, but the textual list contradicts that, which will confuse students about the expected constructor parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification: either (a) update the textual attribute list to match the UML order, or (b) update the UML diagram to match the textual list. Clearly state the exact constructor parameter order in the task description so students and tests have a single unambiguous expectation.

issues.description: The solution implementation provides a Lecture constructor whose parameter order (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) does not follow the attribute order shown in the UML diagram in the problem statement. Since the exercise explicitly instructs students to follow the UML order for the constructor, this discrepancy between the solution and the UML introduces a structural mismatch and may mislead students or tests that expect the UML order.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the Lecture constructor in the solution (and the template) to use the exact parameter order required by the UML diagram, or update the UML to match the constructor order used in solution and template. Ensure the template's constructor signature (if provided) and any tests reflect the agreed-upon order so students implement the constructor consistently with the specification.
